linda-sanchez.text: Voted No on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), motion to concur in the Senate amendment, July 3, 2025; passed 218-214.

source.title: House Roll Call 190, H.R. 1, July 3, 2025 (Clerk of the House)

linda-sanchez.text: Voted against the November 12, 2025 Republican government funding bill because it failed to protect health care subsidies: "I refused to gamble their family budgets on a flimsy promise by the Senate to address these issues later."

source.title: Sánchez stands up for working families, votes against bill that spikes health care premiums

linda-sanchez.text: Said she led Democrats in offering an amendment to block tariffs, citing constituents' "rising health care premiums and grocery costs driven by Trump's reckless tariffs."

source.title: Sánchez stands up for working families, votes against bill that spikes health care premiums

linda-sanchez.text: Campaign statement: "Republicans in Congress have done nothing to address rising costs. ... I'm fighting to lower prices and stand up for the hardworking people who keep our communities running."

source.title: Ballotpedia News: Sánchez and Clemmons compete for CA-41

linda-sanchez.text: Introduced the CHANGE Act (Alzheimer's assessment and diagnosis), which passed the Ways and Means Committee unanimously (September 2026).
Introduced the POWR Act (September 2026) to adjust Social Security survivor benefit calculations for widows and widowers.
Co-sponsored with Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) a bipartisan act to revive U.S. film and television production (September 24, 2026).
Her campaign cites legislation preventing gender-based health insurance discrimination and efforts to improve childcare affordability; former Orange County AFL-CIO executive secretary and treasurer.

mitch-clemmons.text: Campaign position: reduce unnecessary regulation and red tape and "lower barriers that increase housing costs."
Campaign position: reduce the tax burden on families and small businesses and cut unnecessary government spending.
Opposes "climate-focused carbon taxes" and "strict carbon-emissions caps"; supports "targeted, science-based pollution rules."
Emphasizes "securing the U.S. border" and immigration policies "focused on protecting American workers."
Says "schools should educate rather than indoctrinate children" and favors school choice.
Backs legislation "strengthening the traditional family and protecting parents' rights."
Endorsed the SAVE America Act and supports federally mandated proof of citizenship for voting.
Would support additional U.S. military funding if President Trump requested it, tied to clear national-security needs.

notes: Clemmons: no public positions found on health care, abortion, or firearms; his iVoterGuide questionnaire was left unanswered. Clemmons items rely on an aggregator (smarter.vote) summarizing his campaign site. Sánchez: house.gov roll-call/issue pages (clerk.house.gov, congress.gov, govtrack) were mostly blocked (403) for later fetches, so Sánchez items are thinner than ideal.
